title: On Falling into the ditch beside the gate
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：fall　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fall 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the counsellor ① fell into the ditch beside the gate at once, and every listener in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three evenings on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the counsellor ② falls into the ditch beside the gate in the rain without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ fall into the ditch beside the gate at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ fallen into the ditch beside the gate before — a line in the journal for June 1983 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Falling into the ditch beside the gate at once, the counsellor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the letter at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ fall through the rotten board in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Fall through the rotten board at once and never mention it again.

By 1996 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the journal, and a new listener from the next garden ⑧ falls through the rotten board at once every evening without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ fell into the ditch beside the gate again when nobody else would.

⑩ To fall into the ditch beside the gate, my mother said in 2001, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody falls into the ditch beside the gate in the rain again and somebody must fall into the ditch beside the gate at once all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 跌倒（一般过去式 fell into the ditch beside the gate：1989 年谈心人头一回这样做，二话不说地）
B. v. 跌倒（一般现在 falls into the ditch beside the gate：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 跌倒（不定式 to fall into the ditch beside the gate：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 跌倒（过去完成时 had fallen into the ditch beside the gate：1983 年六月的心记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 跌倒（动名词 falling into the ditch beside the gate 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 落下（fall through the rotten board：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去落下从朽了的木板上落下）
G. v. 落下（fall through the rotten board：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 跌倒（后段两处：新来的倾听者照例 falls through the rotten board，而母亲又一次 fell into the ditch beside the gate）

answers.why: fall 意为“跌倒”，1989 年谈心人二话不说地跌倒跌倒在门边的沟里，那是小园里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 fell。
fall 意为“跌倒”，自那以后谈心人淋着雨把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 falls。
fall 意为“跌倒”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯跌倒跌倒在门边的沟里”，此处为不定式 to fall into the ditch beside the gate。
fall 意为“跌倒”，心记里 六月 那行字说明早在 1996 年之前就有人跌倒过，故用过去完成时 had fallen。
fall 意为“跌倒”，谈心人说“跌倒跌倒在门边的沟里这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 falling into the ditch beside the gate 作主语。
fall 意为“落下”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去落下从朽了的木板上落下”，should ever 之后用原形 fall through the rotten board。
fall 意为“落下”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻落下从朽了的木板上落下（fall through the rotten board at once），以后再也不要提起。
fall 意为“跌倒”，新来的倾听者每个黄昏都照例落下从朽了的木板上落下，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 falls。
fall 意为“跌倒”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次二话不说地跌倒跌倒在门边的沟里，用一般过去式 fell 叙述。
fall 意为“跌倒”，结尾那句是母亲 2001 年的话：要跌倒跌倒在门边的沟里，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和小园记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 fall 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1989 the counsellor fell into the ditch beside the gate at once, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the counsellor falls into the ditch beside the gate in the rain whenever the garden asks.
Falling into the ditch beside the gate at once, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever fall through the rotten board in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next garden falls through the rotten board at once every evening, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother fell into the ditch beside the gate again, and the garden remembered that half.
